clue.text: Seekers of justice squirted nerve gas

indicators.note: a squirted liquid sprays out in all directions, so the letters scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: the eight letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Vigilantes spraying nerve gas at their enemies in a revenge attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Avengers punish a wrong done to them or others, so they are people out to get justice.

clue.text: Pick up dress to show off

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it from the bottom, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: Someone collecting a fancy dress just so they can parade in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, talking oneself up to impress others, which is showing off.

clue.text: Money we raised for a tree

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: A fundraising appeal: the money we collected to plant a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical evergreen whose kidney-shaped nuts are eaten, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Enter body of aircraft for start of journey to Pennsylvania Avenue?

definitions.text: start of journey to Pennsylvania Avenue?

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
the cabin is the main passenger section of a plane

explanation.surface: Boarding a plane at the start of a trip to Washington's famous street.
explanation.walkthrough: The White House is at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue; the US myth of rising from a LOG CABIN to the presidency, as Lincoln did, is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Humble birth in a rough timber hut is the traditional American starting point for a path to the presidency.

clue.text: Keeps a stew bubbling — it's a bit of a gamble

indicators.note: a bubbling stew churns its contents about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of the three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook leaving a stew to simmer, unsure how it will turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery-style bet where participants draw horses or teams and the winner takes the pooled stakes.

clue.text: One palace in two dioceses

parts.note: the first diocese: Ely is a cathedral city and bishopric in Cambridgeshire
the second diocese: a see is a bishop's area of authority

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a single palace that somehow lies within two bishops' territories.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. 'One palace' marks a particular palace, so a proper name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée in Paris is the official residence of the French president, a single named palace.

clue.text: Create too much suspense in project

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: to hang something excessively, to suspend it too far
second meaning: to jut out beyond what is below

explanation.surface: A writer or film-maker spinning out the tension in a project.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful reading: 'suspense' as suspension, 'too much' as over, so hang over-far.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge or roof that sticks out beyond its base is said to jut or protrude beyond the wall.

clue.text: Hamburger, say, one that infects a number

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that causes infection
taken as written
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A food-safety scare: a burger carrying bacteria that make many people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is a person from Hamburg, not a sandwich; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the city of Hamburg is an example of a person from Germany.

clue.text: Man, old, was suffering

indicators.note: something suffering is in a poor or broken state, so these letters are knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man who was in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald is a male first name, so it can stand for any man so named.

clue.text: Comfy as an insect in a carpet?

parts.words: as an insect in a carpet?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about how a bug living in the pile of a rug feels

parts.words: Comfy as an insect in a carpet?
parts.note: setter's reading: the clue completes the saying about a bug in a rug, whose first word means cosy

explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'as snug as a bug in a rug', meaning very cosy; the clue swaps in synonyms for bug and rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes being warm, cosy and comfortable, so it fits the adjective comfy.

clue.text: Cheddar is too bad

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a firm, pressed cheese, of which Cheddar is an example
second meaning: a British idiom offering mock sympathy for bad luck

explanation.surface: A cheese lover's verdict that this particular Cheddar is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang said to someone who has had bad luck, often unsympathetically.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a firm, pressed type of dairy product, and the exclamation 'hard luck' means the same as too bad.

clue.text: Give some bribes to warden

indicators.note: only some of the following words are wanted, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Advice on corrupting a prison guard by slipping them a few bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present or confer something as a gift, which is to give it.

clue.text: Criterion for judging fool on stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a standard against which others are measured
second meaning: the jester in Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's standard for assessing a comic actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A touchstone was originally a dark stone used to test gold; Shakespeare named his clown after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone is a benchmark or test of quality, and the court jester in As You Like It bears this name.

clue.text: Taken by surprise, confess to being exhausted

parts.note: owning up to being something means saying 'I am'
bushed is informal for very tired

explanation.surface: Someone caught off guard admits they are simply worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushed means attacked or caught unexpectedly from hiding, so caught unawares.

clue.text: Robust door finally installed in workroom

indicators.note: something installed in a room is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a study is a room for working in

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solid new door fitted at last in someone's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means strongly built and hard to damage, the same as robust.

clue.text: At sea, guard the offspring

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the eight letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: An order on board ship to keep watch over the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child of her parents, one kind of offspring.

clue.text: Home leave, only a little

parts.note: being in means being at home
to part is to leave or go away

explanation.surface: Someone granted only a small amount of time off to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: In part means partly or to some extent, so only to a small degree.

clue.text: Excellent shirt, not check?

parts.note: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a shirt
taken as written
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict on a shirt that is plain rather than chequered.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is informal for first-rate, of the highest quality, so it means excellent.

clue.text: Senior cleric keeping care of a junior one

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A high-ranking churchman looking after one of his subordinates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to cleric, so the definition is a junior cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest, so a lower-ranking member of the clergy.

clue.text: Seat that you filled in serious cinema

indicators.note: a seat that is filled has something placed inside it

parts.note: slang for the backside, what one sits on
the old form of you

explanation.surface: An usher's question about who sat in a chair at a highbrow film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' means the backside, not a chair; 'that you filled' says the seat is filled by the old word for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthouse films are artistic, non-commercial movies shown in specialist venues, intellectual rather than mainstream fare.

clue.text: Bear name of rugby forward

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
pert means cheeky, bold

explanation.surface: Telling someone the name of a rugby team's forward player.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character, a bear in checked trousers. 'Forward' means cheeky, not a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous British cartoon character called Rupert is a bear, so this is a name for a bear.

clue.text: Pile into business that's worth little

indicators.note: into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: Someone sinking money into a firm that turns out to be almost worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for cheap and shoddy, something of low value or quality.

clue.text: About to go astray ending with nothing here, I bet

parts.note: ca, for circa, means about
to sin is to go morally astray
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gambler admitting they are about to lose their way and end up with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a place: 'here' is where I place a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people gamble, so it is where someone would place wagers.

clue.text: Random scans for measles?

parts.note: setter's reading: unannounced inspections made on a sample basis
surface reading: a doctor examining a patient for the rash of a childhood illness

explanation.walkthrough: Measles produces a rash of red spots, so a doctor checking for it would literally look for spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Unannounced inspections chosen at random are what this phrase means in everyday use.

clue.text: Feminine, quiet, gliding movement

parts.note: F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine
a low voice is a quiet one

explanation.surface: A description of a graceful, hushed dancer drifting across a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow is a smooth, steady, continuous motion, like a liquid moving along easily.

clue.text: That's your lot!

parts.note: surface reading: the everyday British phrase for 'that's all there is, nothing more'
setter's reading: one's lot in life, what destiny allots

explanation.walkthrough: 'That's your lot' is British slang meaning that's all you are getting; lot also means destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or portion in life, the share decided by chance or providence.

clue.text: The colour of an old house

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shade between red and yellow
second meaning: the European royal dynasty of William III

explanation.surface: Asking what shade a historic building was painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a royal dynasty, not a building: the House of Orange reigned in the Netherlands and gave Britain William III.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour named after the fruit, and also the name of the Dutch princely dynasty.

clue.text: He cannot work out modern engineering

indicators.note: to work something out is to rework it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters of the two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A baffled person unable to understand present-day technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanotechnology manipulates matter at the atomic scale, a recent branch of applied science.
